scenario.name: PwC, CrowdStrike & Elastic DFIR — Linux BPFDoor Raw Socket Filter, /dev/shm Masquerading & /proc/net/packet Forensics
scenario.overview: Imagine a phantom eavesdropper inside a railway telegraph depot who moves into a temporary memory-only closet, shreds the paper entry receipt, puts on a station-cleaner badge, and clips an invisible wire sieve directly onto the main incoming telegraph cable so no open door appears on the depot map. During an emergency audit, a forensic inspector bypasses the front floor map completely, reads the raw cable-tap ledger, and uncovers both the invisible sieve and the brass locking pin keeping it alone. In this scenario (T1036.004, PwC, CrowdStrike & Elastic DFIR, Linux BPFDoor Raw Socket Filter, /dev/shm Masquerading & /proc/net/packet Forensics), the attacker follows one continuous intrusion path so each later Step can show the exact handoff that makes the next stage possible. The attack unfolds in one continuous arc: memory-Backed /dev/shm Execution, then raw Packet Socket Creation, then forensic Discovery via /proc/net/packet, ss. Steps #1–#3 walk that chain end-to-end by covering Memory-Backed /dev/shm Execution, then Raw Packet Socket Creation, then Forensic Discovery via /proc/net/packet, ss, while the Process Hierarchy tab keeps the Parent → Child spawn tree visible so you can see which trusted process launched the next payload. Primary detection pivots on auditd Event 59 correlated across the documented kill chain.

stages.title: Stage 1: Memory-Backed /dev/shm Execution, Self-Deletion & /proc/<pid>/exe (deleted) Artifact
stages.subtitle: Defense Evasion (T1036.004 - Masquerading: Masquerade Task or Service)
stages.description: At launch, the eavesdropper dashes into a memory-only storage closet, tears up the closet doorway sign so disk inventories find nothing, and alters its own staff nametag to resemble a harmless background maintenance utility. Upon startup, the implant copies its binary into tmpfs shared memory (/dev/shm/kdmtmpflush), executes the copy with --init, overwrites its command-line argv[0] via prctl(PR_SET_NAME) to mimic a kernel thread ("[kdmtmpflush]"), and unlinks the file from /dev/shm. steps.plainTitle: Raw Packet Socket Creation & Classic BPF Bytecode Attachment (SO_ATTACH_FILTER)
steps.storyAnalogy: Instead of opening a numbered ticket window that every night watchman checks, the eavesdropper clamps a raw acoustic sieve straight onto the main telegraph line so every passing signal is inspected silently until a secret trigger code arrives.
